purpose: Identity-resolution failure rate of weebcentral_client.resolve() across a popularity-stratified MAL manga sample.
titleFieldQueried: title_english || title (matches Colosseum app read shape)

summary.refused_no_match_definition: WeebCentral returned candidates but the best scored < 0.8 -- the threshold / romaji-vs-English question.
summary.refused_no_result_definition: WeebCentral's search returned ZERO candidates for the query -- genuinely absent, or the query needs the romaji title.
summary.resolved_near_floor_contains_wrong_serie: TRUE POSITIVE for the load-bearing role of the 0.8 floor: 'Kanon'->'Kanokon' scored 0.8333 and was ACCEPTED as resolved. Kanon (Key) is NOT Kanokon. The current 0.8 floor already lets at least one wrong-series match through; lowering it would admit more.

refusalAnalysis.obviousCandidateDefinition: a refused_no_match whose best WeebCentral candidate scored > 0.0 (a real candidate existed, just below threshold -- confirmable by a stronger signal like chapter count or alternate titles; NOT a model judgement).
refusalAnalysis.nearThreshold_definition: best score >= 0.5 (clustered near the 0.8 floor -- a THRESHOLD question, tunable by lowering MATCH_THRESHOLD).
refusalAnalysis.nearZero_definition: best score < 0.5 (romaji-vs-English territory -- no string comparison solves this; needs alternate-title data).
refusalAnalysis.obviousCandidate_definition_RETRACTED: METRIC RETRACTED. 'best score > 0.0' is NOT an obvious-correct signal -- it only means some string overlap, which includes wrong-series hits (e.g. 'Chicago'->'Chichi-Chichi' 0.42, 'Oouso Swing'->'Ookiku-Furikabutte' 0.30 = Big Windup!). Declaring a candidate 'obvious correct' would require a model/external signal, which is out of scope (no LLM in the data path). The score-band split (near-threshold vs near-zero) is the honest data; per-band eyeball characterization is in the report prose.

sameSeries_differentName_examples: Little Witch Academia -> Little-Witch-Academia-satou-Keisuke (different adaptation manga by a different author)
Neon Genesis Evangelion: The Shinji Ikari Raising Project -> exact prefix match, different subtitle
wrongSeries_examples: Suicide Parabellum -> Parabellum (different manga sharing a word)
Sakura Irony -> Sakuran (different series, shared stem)
Sword of the Stranger -> sword-of-the-titans (shared word only)
Sayonara no Jikan -> Sayonara-Nippon (shared word only)
nearThreshold_0.7_to_0.8_eyeball.characterization: MIXED. Even the highest refusal band is NOT cleanly 'same series, tunable'. Roughly half are same-series/different-name (adaptation variants, spinoffs); the other half are wrong-series sharing a word. Lowering the threshold to catch the first half would ALSO admit the second half -- confirmed by the resolved set: 'Kanon'->'Kanokon' (0.833) is a WRONG-SERIES match the current floor already accepts.
